formalDefinition: 3SAT = {Φ | Φ is a satisfiable Boolean formula in 3CNF}
problemDefinition: 3SAT is the Boolean satisfiability problem restricted to formulas in conjunctive normal form with at most three literals per clause. It asks whether there is an assignment of True/False values to the variables of Φ that makes the whole formula True.
outputDescription: True or False, whether Φ is satisfiable
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
instanceFormat: Boolean formula in 3-CNF. Clauses joined by '&', literals within a clause joined by '|', negation prefix '!'. Each clause has at most 3 literals. Example: (x1 | !x2 | x3) & (!x1 | x3 | x1)
certificateFormat: Comma-separated variable:Boolean pairs, optionally wrapped in parentheses. Booleans must be capitalized True/False (T/F also accepted); ':' or '=' may be used as the separator. List every variable you are assigning. Example: (x1:True,x2:False,x3:True)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a O(2^n) solution algorithm for the 3SAT problem which implements a back tracking algorithm to find an exact assignment boolean assignment of variables to satisfy the problem instance.
defaultSolver.complexity: O(2^n * |phi|), n = number of variables, |phi| = formula size

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for 3SAT. It takes the certificate from the user and validates that every clause contains a true literal

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for 3SAT
